body: `idpById` comes from `getById()`, which returns the org-aware wrapper whose `isEnabled()` is false whenever the linked organization (or the org feature) is disabled. The login predicate is then evaluated against org state, but the JPA `getForLogin` query that fills the cache ignores org state, so disabled-org IDPs are still in the cached lists. This can leave the cache stale. Example: org is disabled, and IDP X is linked, public and enabled, so it is in the cached ORG_ONLY/ALL lists. An admin sets `hideOnLogin=true` on X. The wrapped `original` fails the predicate because `isEnabled()` is false, and `updated` fails it because of hideOnLogin, so the early return skips invalidation. When the org is re-enabled, X still comes back from the cache, and `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` only re-checks `isEnabled()`, so the hidden IDP appears on the login page. Evaluate the predicate on the unwrapped stored model instead, e.g. `idpDelegate.getById(model.getInternalId())`, as `remove()` already does with `idpDelegate.getByAlias`.

Adding the org/BROKER_PUBLIC clause to `getLoginPredicate()` changes more than cache invalidation. `IdentityProviderBean.federatedProviderPredicate()` returns this predicate, and it is used when organizations are disabled for the realm or feature. A user whose federated identity comes from an IDP that is still linked to an org but not marked public used to see that IDP on the login page and no longer will. To limit the change to cache invalidation, keep the public API predicate as it was and put the org/public check in a separate predicate used only by the Infinispan provider.

Cached entries are resolved through `getById()`, which returns org-aware wrappers whose `isEnabled()` depends on the org's current enabled state. So the correctness of the cached list depends on every caller re-filtering with `isEnabled()`. `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` was patched to do this. But `IdentityProviderBean.searchForIdentityProviders` (REALM_ONLY) and any other `getForLogin` consumer, including custom extensions, do not re-check, and the SPI javadoc says the method returns IDPs 'suitable for being displayed in the login pages'. Either filter `isEnabled()` here before returning, or document that callers must re-check it.

For `REALM_ONLY`, the delegate ignores `organizationId`, but the search key still includes it. Each distinct orgId passed with REALM_ONLY creates a new sub-entry holding the same result. Worse, every miss on an existing entry runs the `invalidateObject` + re-add path, which evicts and rebuilds the whole query. Normalize the search key to "" when `mode == REALM_ONLY`.

The cleanup removes the hard-coded alias "alias", not `idpRep.getAlias()`, so none of the 20 IDPs created here (or idp-alias-20 below) are removed after the test. This can leak state into other tests in the class. The same problem is at the second `addCleanup` further down.
